# Startup readback: AI-45

Contract version: 1

## Objective and acceptance outcomes

AI-45 makes evidence and backups recoverable across PostgreSQL and private R2. Remaining outcomes are: (1) export a database/migration checkpoint and every referenced archive object with private/encrypted storage, integrity metadata, and unchanged original bytes; (2) restore into a clean isolated target, preserving critical relational links and proving an application-readable archived trace/evidence/report; and (3) detect a missing/corrupt disposable object clearly, prove the source is unchanged, and keep the RPO/RTO and manual path documented. No live sign-off is claimed until the staging-source proof and isolated application-read journey pass.

## Dependencies and relevant contracts

AI-9, AI-19, and AI-65 are Done. AI-65 confirms environment-separated R2 prerequisites and safe canaries; that result is not application restore proof. AI-19 owns trace/evidence metadata. AI-45 remains In Review. Its latest live readiness note says source and backup R2 credentials passed safe bucket checks and the dedicated versioned encryption key is configured; an earlier isolated round trip still had zero archived traces and zero linked evidence rows. No third hosted Supabase project is assumed: the guarded local-recovery path uses a separate local Supabase stack and loopback-only S3-compatible archive. Follow Build Spec §§5.4, 6.2–6.4, 10.1–10.6; Agent Spec §§9.2, 10.2–10.3; and the Frontend Constitution's linked-evidence and blocked/permission/error states. Main offers `archive-restore` in `.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml` but omits it from `infrastructure/scripts/release-gate.ts`; preserve all current profiles while completing selector → evidence producer → strict schema → release consumer/status. Integration rules R2-01, R2-02, and ACC-10 apply.

## Implementation and boundaries

This refresh first repairs the mainline release contract: use an explicit archive-restore selector, preserve the seven required outcomes and exact deployment/candidate provenance through the hosted evidence schema, and ensure the canonical consumer cannot mark pending, malformed, or wrong-run evidence accepted. Retain every profile already on main. Port the established AI-45 archive, backup, and isolated-restore implementation from PR #175 only after this readback is checked; resolve shared files against current main without touching the old or dirty Temp worktrees. Keep the finance gateway GET/read-back and verified marker, owner-scoped fresh-MFA archive retrieval, AES-256-GCM backup, production-restore refusal, and separate local-recovery safeguards. Use synthetic data only; never restore production or expose credentials.

## Local tests and commands

First run selector and release-gate tests for all profile variants, including seven archive-restore outcomes, missing-outcome rejection, wrong candidate/deployment binding, pending-state preservation, and workflow producer compatibility. Then run focused backup-integrity/restore and archive-gateway tests: encrypted round trip, invalid key/envelope, absent/extra/truncated/hash-mismatched object, read-back mismatch, owner scope, and fresh-MFA authorization. After integrating the candidate, run `corepack pnpm verify:changed`. PR #175 reports prior focused tests and CI green on an older head; those do not prove the refreshed mainline profile or latest code.

## Hosted proof and readiness

No current-turn staging-source backup/restore has run, and no live sign-off is claimed. Once the parent grants the staging slot, use synthetic staging data, the existing private archive/backup buckets and versioned key, and the isolated local recovery target. Prove linked rows, trace/evidence/report retrieval, exact original bytes, disposable corruption detection, and unchanged source. Do not provision another hosted Supabase project or use production data. A fresh MFA-gated archived-evidence read may require the operator to complete a visible-browser sign-in/MFA handoff. Final release still requires merge and bounded affected-capability production smoke; never restore over production.

## Delegation and blockers

One owner remains accountable through merge. The parent owns the shared staging lease and release schedule; AI-27 owns the shared local database, so this lane uses non-DB proofs until that lease is explicitly released. Root `qa:doctor --fix` is green for this pass and will not be rerun concurrently. Current blockers are the linked-archive isolated restore proof, exact-head checks, staging acceptance, and release/production gates. If the UI requests real-account sign-in/MFA, stop before acting and hand off the visible browser to the operator.
